title: Vulnerable package version detected
detect: A newly added or updated npm package is pinned to a version with a known CVE. Prefer the injected npm audit results as ground truth; never assert a CVE that is not in that audit output.

title: Unpinned or wildcard dependency version
detect: A production dependency uses ^, ~, or * instead of an exact version, allowing a silently vulnerable patch release to be pulled in at install time.

title: New package with no community trust signals
detect: A brand-new or obscure dependency is added (very low downloads, no repo, recently published). Flag for manual supply-chain review; cannot be confirmed from the diff alone.
secure_example: // Prefer a well-established alternative; verify downloads, stars, maintainer history

title: Dependency confusion / typosquatting risk
detect: An added package name is a near-match to a popular or internal package (possible typosquat). Suspect but verify against the registry; do not confirm from the diff alone.
secure_example: // Verify the exact package name on npmjs.com; use: npm info <package>

title: SQL / NoSQL injection via string interpolation
detect: A query is built by concatenating or interpolating user input instead of using parameterized queries or ORM methods. Applies to raw pg queries, Sequelize query(), and Knex raw().
insecure_example:
const q = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}'`
await db.query(q)
secure_example: await db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email=$1', [req.body.email])

title: Command injection via exec / spawn
detect: User input is passed to child_process.exec, execSync, or spawn with shell:true, allowing arbitrary command execution.

title: Hardcoded secrets or credentials
detect: An API key, DB password, JWT secret, or other credential is hardcoded in source instead of being loaded from an environment variable.
secure_example:
const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET
if (!JWT_SECRET) throw new Error('Missing JWT_SECRET')

title: Path traversal in file operations
detect: A user-supplied filename or path is used directly in an fs operation without resolving and validating it against an allowed base directory.
insecure_example:
const file = req.params.name
fs.readFile('./uploads/' + file, cb)

title: Sensitive data in error responses
detect: A stack trace, DB error message, or internal path is returned to the client instead of a generic error message.

title: Missing rate limiting on sensitive endpoints
detect: The diff introduces a login, password-reset, OTP, or registration endpoint with no rate limiting. Absence rule: only flag when the diff adds the endpoint and no limiter is present in the diff; the limiter may exist elsewhere, so mark as verify.

title: Prototype pollution via object merge
detect: A user-supplied object is merged with Object.assign or _.merge without key validation, allowing prototype pollution.

title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user content
detect: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used with user-supplied or API-sourced data without sanitization, enabling XSS.

title: Sensitive data stored in localStorage
detect: A JWT, session token, or PII is stored in localStorage, where any XSS payload can read it. localStorage is acceptable only for non-sensitive UI state.
secure_example:
// Auth token: httpOnly cookie set by server
localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark') // non-sensitive only

title: API keys or secrets in frontend bundle
detect: A private API key or secret is placed in a frontend env var (e.g. REACT_APP_*), which ships to the client.

title: Open redirect via user-controlled navigation
detect: window.location.href or navigate(url) is set from a query param or user input without validating against an allowlist of internal paths.

title: Raw ORM query with interpolated input
detect: sequelize.query(), TypeORM query(), or Knex raw() is called with a template literal or string concatenation, bypassing ORM parameterization.
secure_example: sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = :id', { replacements: { id: userId } })

title: Missing authorization scope on data queries
detect: A record is fetched by ID without scoping to the authenticated user (IDOR). Absence rule: flag when the diff adds a by-ID fetch with no ownership clause; scoping may occur elsewhere, so mark as verify.
secure_example: const order = await Order.findOne({ where: { id: req.params.id, userId: req.user.id } })

title: Unbounded query on large table
detect: A findAll or SELECT * has no LIMIT/pagination on a table that can grow large, a DoS and data-exposure risk.
secure_example: const users = await User.findAll({ limit: parseInt(req.query.limit) || 20, offset: parseInt(req.query.offset) || 0 })

title: Sensitive columns returned in default scope
detect: A query returns a model whose default scope includes sensitive fields (password_hash, 2fa_secret, ssn) without excluding them. Needs the model definition, which may not be in the diff; mark as verify.
insecure_example:
const user = await User.findByPk(id)
res.json(user) // includes password_hash
secure_example: const user = await User.findByPk(id, { attributes: { exclude: ['passwordHash','twoFaSecret'] } })

title: JWT verified without algorithm pinning
detect: jwt.verify is called without an explicit algorithms option, allowing the alg:none / algorithm-confusion bypass.

title: Authorization check only at route level
detect: A role/permission check exists only in route middleware with no enforcement at the service/data layer. Absence rule spanning files; mark as verify.
insecure_example: router.get('/admin/users', requireAdmin, handler) // handler has no ownership check

title: Password hashed with weak or no algorithm
detect: A password is stored using MD5, SHA-1, unsalted SHA-256, or plaintext instead of bcrypt (cost >= 12), Argon2id, or scrypt.

title: Missing CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints
detect: A cookie-session, state-changing endpoint is added without CSRF protection or Origin/Referer verification. Absence rule; mark as verify.
insecure_example: app.post('/transfer', isAuthenticated, transferHandler) // no CSRF token

title: dotenv / .env file committed to repo
detect: The PR adds a .env, .env.production, or .env.local file with real credentials. Detectable from the changed filenames.

title: Security headers not set
detect: An Express app is created with no security-header middleware (helmet). Absence rule across the app; mark as verify.
insecure_example: const app = express() // no security headers

title: CORS configured with wildcard origin
detect: CORS is configured with origin:'*', especially together with credentials:true, allowing any site to make authenticated cross-origin requests.
